Per: Justice Avanindra Kumar Singh This appeal under Section 415 of Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is filed by appellant-Mohit Kumar Rajak, being aggrieved of the judgment dated 22/05/2025 passed by the learned Special Judge (POCSO Act), Singrauli (M.P.) in SC No.04/2023,
whereby the appellant has been convicted for offences under sections 363, 366, 376(3) & 376(2)(N)
of IPC and 3/4(2) & 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act and

sentenced as under :-
Conviction u/s Imprisonment (RI) Fine amount In lieu of 366 of IPC RI for 7 years Rs.500/- RI for 1 year 3/4(2) of POCSO Act RI for 20 years Rs.500/- RI for 1 year 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act RI for 20 years Rs.500/- RI for 1 year 2.

In short, the case of the prosecution is that on 25/12/2022 at about 12:21 hours, mother of the prosecutrix has lodged the report at Police NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50837 2 CRA-5673-2025 Station, Vindhyanagar that her daughter who is aged about 15 years and studying in Class-IX on 23.12.2020 at around 10 pm after having meals slept alongwith her sister.

1 Rajak, she was informed that her daughter eloped with Mohit Rajak.
On the basis of above complaint, Police registered FIR No.613/2022 for offence u/s 363 IPC against the appellant.
3. During investigation documents regarding date of birth of the victim were seized and Missing Person Report in respect of victim was recorded.

After recovery of victim, 'Dastiyabi Panchnama'
was prepared and she was handed-over to her mother.
The victim was medically examined, spot inspection was done and spot map was prepared.
After arrest of accused, he was also medically examined and charge-sheet was filed in Court.

4. Accused was charged for offences under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) & 376(2)(N) of IPC and 3/4(2)
& 5(L)/6 of POCSO Act, who abjured his guilt, pleaded innocence and claimed trial.
5. The prosecution examined total 14 witnesses including victim/prosecutrix as PW-1, whereas defence examined accused as DW-1.
After prosecution the accused in his examination under Section 313 of Cr.P.C., denied the prosecution evidence and stated his false implication.

6. Learned trial Court on the basis of oral and documentary evidence available on record held the appellant guilty of the aforesaid offences and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50837 3 CRA-5673-2025 convicted & sentenced, as has been stated hereinabove.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant has challenged the impugned judgment of conviction and sentenced on the ground that there are material contradictions and omissions in the prosecution evidence.
On the date of incident the victim was not less than 18 years and was consenting party.

Therefore, impugned judgment of conviction is liable to be set aside and appellant be acquitted of the charges levelled against him.
8.
Learned Government Advocate has supported the impugned judgment and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

9. Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.
10.
Prosecutrix (PW-1) in her statement has stated that her date of birth is 04/09/2008.
In Para-7 of her cross-examination, she stated that she cannot say whether age of her elder sister Anita is 28 years.
But in Para-15, she stated that it is true to say that she is 6 years younger than Anita.

11. Mother of the prosecutrix (PW-6) has stated that when she went to get admission of the prosecutrix in school then Principal was not recorded the age of the prosecutrix as stated by her,
therefore she went to counsellor Ramkaya Kushwaha who give a certificate on letterhead and on that basis, age of the prosecutrix in school was recorded as 04/09/2008.
In Para-7 of her cross-examination, she stated that she has five children.
She does not know the date of birth of her children but all were born at an interval of 2 -2 years.
The name of her eldest daughter is Anita and second daughter is Sunita.

sentences.text: Father of the prosecutrix (PW-7) has stated that date of birth of the prosecutrix is 04/09/2008.

In Para-4 of his cross-examination, he stated NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50837 4 CRA-5673-2025 that age was recorded in the school on the basis of certificate of the Parshad and it is correct to say that since there was no document regarding date of birth of the prosecutrix, hence Parshad Ramkaya Kushwaha by estimation mentioned the age in the certificate which was recorded in school and which is being mentioned in the Court.
13. Mudrika Prasad Dubey, Principal (PW-2) stated that on the basis of scholar register, the date of birth of the prosecutrix is 04/09/2008.
It is not mentioned as to on what basis, the date of birth is mentioned in school record.
14. Dr. Sarita Shah (PW-3) has stated that on medical examination, it was found that secondary sexual characters of the prosecutrix were well developed.

She stated that on medical examination,
hymen of the prosecutrix was found to be old torn but there was no evidence of forceful intercourse.
15.

Looking to the evidence regarding age of the prosecutrix, it is found that the age of the prosecutrix was recorded by estimation in school and there was no reliable document regarding age of the prosecutrix.
Hence, it is found that prosecution has failed to establish that on the date of incident i.e. 24/12/2022 prosecutrix was minor and was less than 18 years of age.

Accordingly,
finding recorded by the trial Court in this regard in Para-26 be set aside for the reasons mentioned above.

16. Since, it is not proved that the prosecutrix (PW-1) was to be less than 18 years of age on the date of incident i.e. on 24/12/2022 and looking to the statement of the prosecutrix (PW-1) in which she stated that she went on her own volition with the accused and had developed physical relation on her NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50837 5 CRA-5673-2025 own consent and got married and her statement that on the phone call of the accused, that let us go for tour, therefore without informing her parents she went with the accused on motorcycle to Bargava, thereafter came back to Navanagar and stayed there for sometime.
Then they went by a bus to Sidhi, Rewa and Satna, from where by train they went to Surajpur (C.G.) where accused made physical relation with her consent (as per Para -3 of examination-in-chief).
Thereafter, on 28th they went to a temple and got married.
In Para-8 of her cross-examination, she stated that she liked the accused and known him for about 8-9 months.
In Para-12 she stated that when her mother saw her talking with the accused on phone, then she was assaulted by her.
Therefore, no offence are proved against the appellant in which conviction and sentence has been passed by the trial Court as mentioned above.
17. Accordingly, appeal is allowed.
The impugned judgment dated 22/05/2025 passed by learned trial Court is set aside.
18. Appellant be released forthwith, if not required in any other case.
Case property be disposed off in terms of the orders of the learned trial Court.
Record of the learned trial Court be sent back.
(VIVEK AGARWAL)
